label: Third input step (t=2) when token 1 is in {g,q,y,a,u} and token 2 is in {a,b,d,g,i,l,q,s,u,v,w,y}
explanation: Fires only at step t=2, the third original token. It fires there only when the first original token is one of g/q/y/a/u and the second is one of a,b,d,g,i,l,q,s,u,v,w,y. The token at step 2 itself barely matters. Every (first, second) pair inside these sets fires with near-100% precision. Within a few weak pairs (a-w, u-w, a-q, u-u) it fires only part of the time. Magnitude depends on the first token: g and q are strongest (about 0.35 of activation mass each), y is intermediate, and a and u are weak. Weak activations (<0.1 of max) also appear when the first token is b; that case holds 0.5% of mass. Never fires at any other step, at the delimiter, in the copy phase, or when token 2 is a digit or a letter outside the set.

issues: Minor: the misses are almost all first_tok=b at t=2 with a second token in the set. They are weak (mostly <0.05 of max, one 0.13) and hold 0.5% of mass, as the explanation says. Adding b to the first-token set gives recall 1.0 but drops precision to 0.84 (test F1 0.913), so leaving it out is the better choice.

Minor: the false positives sit in the weak a/u pairs (u-w, u-q, a-q, a-w), as the explanation says. Excluding a/u x {w,q,u} gives precision 1.0 but recall 0.895 (test F1 0.945), which is worse than the original 0.966.
